name: Tapo P105

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). Bluetooth is used for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings for the P105 and doesn't mention Matter, but never says it has none. TP-Link's Matter plugs carry an M suffix (e.g. P125M).

apple_home.note: TP-Link's P105 platform list names Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, not HomeKit, but doesn't rule it out.

google_home.note: Link the Tapo account in the Google Home app or from the Tapo app.

alexa.note: Link the Tapo account through the Tapo skill.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings among the P105's platforms.

home_assistant.note: The official TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P105. Tapo devices need your TP-Link account credentials to authenticate.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; TP-Link says no hub is required.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's integration talks to the plug on the local network. The Tapo app itself goes through the cloud.

energyMonitoring.note: TP-Link says the P110 and P115 measure energy; the P100 and P105 don't.

maxLoadWatts.note: 15 A, 1800 W at 120 V general use / resistive load; 1/6 HP motor. The US page gives 100–125 V input; the 2020 datasheet and some boxes say 100–240 V.

summary: TP-Link's Tapo P105 is a mini US plug for Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings, each linked through your Tapo account. Home Assistant's official TP-Link integration supports it too and controls it on your local network. It joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly, using Bluetooth only for setup, and is rated 15 A / 1800 W. Two gaps: no energy monitoring, and TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter.
caveats: No energy monitoring; TP-Link says the P110 and P115 are the Tapo plugs that measure power.
TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter; its Matter plugs carry an M suffix, such as the P125M.
Home Assistant needs your TP-Link account credentials to authenticate Tapo devices.
Motor loads are limited to 1/6 HP.
